keyFindings.description: A session name an entry fixes is bound to the pod uid or the workflow run, so the next run of a fixed-session workflow and the replacement pod of a fixed-session account are refused invalid_grant until the previous claim lapses (a still-renewing old pod holds it indefinitely). Proven with a throwaway test on Postgres: both 400 invalid_grant 'Another identity is writing under the session name'.

Security[authz]: a session name is held only while its holder keeps exchanging. Once the claim lapses (the access lifetime, 15 minutes by default) any listed identity takes it: a throwaway test showed another project's pod getting 200 and a token introspecting session=<the first pod's session>, person=its own, project=OTHER, after which the first pod's renewal is refused. A dev box may name any session, including one an entry fixes. The binding also expires before the token it is made for (deep-review). The PR body's 'held by the identity that first claimed it' overstates what the code holds.

The library wraps a storage failure in ErrRequestUnauthorized (401), so Introspect answers a database outage as {active:false} with 200 instead of the 503 and error log its own comment and the route promise.

Security[authz]: the machine access-token exchange does not lock and check the launcher credential the way machine.Service.Live does for the device grant, so an exchange racing a revoke commits a live 15-minute token after the revoke ended the machine's tokens.

No '## Contract change census' although the change adds boot refusals (BROKER_UI_TOKEN[_FILE], DISPATCH_AGENT_SECRETS_TOKEN[_FILE]), moves every broker approval route from the shared bearer to BROKER_API_ACCOUNTS, drops UI_INVALID, and removes the envoy-infra Dispatch component input agentSecretsTokenSecret, which the deployment repository's dispatch/main.go passes today. The rollout line must say how approvals behave between the broker's deploy and Dispatch's, which are separate deploys.
